prioritized_investigations.title: Class-Support Stratification and Primary Metric Sensitivity Diagnostic
prioritized_investigations.diagnostic_question: Does DEV class-support imbalance make the primary macro-mIoU estimate disproportionately sensitive to a small number of physical acquisitions, and how much does the interpretation change when results are stratified by class support?
prioritized_investigations.target_failure: Disproportionate sensitivity of unweighted macro mIoU to sparse-support classes in DEV (e.g. classes with 1-3 scenes), where individual acquisitions have high leverage on class-level estimates.
existing_evidence: In OPS-02 DEV, Class 5 (OF) appears in exactly 1 sample (0.067% pixels), Class 7 (RF) in 2 samples (0.372% pixels), and Class 11 (HM) in 3 samples (0.005% pixels).

Sparse class support in the DEV partition may reduce the reliability and stability of class-level IoU estimates, because individual scenes contribute disproportionately to the metric. This is a measurement-support concern, not a mathematical upper bound on macro mIoU.
Major classes (MCC, IWs) achieve consistently nonzero performance with observed class IoU means of 0.21-0.26 (MCC) and 0.10-0.23 (IWs), though between-seed variability remains present.
prioritized_investigations.why_it_resolves_uncertainty: Evaluates whether DEV class-support imbalance makes the primary macro-mIoU estimate disproportionately sensitive to a small number of physical acquisitions, and quantifies how interpretation changes when results are stratified by class support (using support-stratified summaries as descriptive secondary diagnostics without altering the frozen primary metric).
prioritized_investigations.scientific_cost: Very Low (purely post-hoc statistical re-analysis of existing evaluation tensors).
prioritized_investigations.compute_cost: ZERO GPU compute (CPU-only analysis of existing checkpoint prediction masks).
prioritized_investigations.risk_of_confounding: Minimal (no retraining, no dataset mutation, primary metric unchanged).
prioritized_investigations.expected_information_value: Extremely High (clarifies whether the observed ~0.05 mIoU reflects broad model behavior or sparse-support estimator variance).
prioritized_investigations.required_control: Existing evaluated DEV confusion matrices and per-scene IoU breakdowns across Seeds 42, 101, 202, 303, 404.
prioritized_investigations.required_data: Existing OPS-02 DEV split and stored run predictions.

prioritized_investigations.title: Candidate F Hybrid Sampler Schedule Exposure and Seed-Variance Audit
prioritized_investigations.diagnostic_question: Does the realized Candidate F sampling schedule produce materially different class/parent exposure patterns across seeds that are associated with the observed performance variance?
prioritized_investigations.target_failure: High between-seed performance volatility on moderately rare classes (BS, POW, Eddy).
existing_evidence: BS IoU spans 0.018 to 0.158 across seeds in Control (8.6x variance).
POW IoU spans 0.003 to 0.102 across seeds in Control (34x variance).
Eddy IoU spans 0.000 to 0.102 across seeds in Control.
The model and dataset are 100% bitwise identical; only the random seed driving the Candidate F schedule (72 draws/epoch with replacement from 132 samples) differs.
prioritized_investigations.why_it_resolves_uncertainty: Directly measures the empirical distribution of per-class and per-parent tile exposures across epochs for each random seed, testing whether realized Candidate F sampling draw schedules correlate descriptively with between-seed performance variance, without assuming a causal starvation mechanism or modifying the sampler.
prioritized_investigations.compute_cost: ZERO GPU compute (analyzes precomputed Candidate F index schedules and manifest sample labels).
prioritized_investigations.expected_information_value: High (identifies whether realized sampler schedule variance correlates with validation performance differences without changing architecture or data).
prioritized_investigations.required_control: Precomputed Candidate F sampler draw schedules for Seeds 42, 101, 202, 303, 404.

prioritized_investigations.title: Single-Band VV SAR Radiometric Contrast and Distributional Overlap Audit
prioritized_investigations.diagnostic_question: Assess whether class-conditional backscatter distributions in the available single-band VV input exhibit substantial overlap that could plausibly limit discriminability.
prioritized_investigations.target_failure: Persistent zero-IoU on RF (0.00000 across all 10 runs), HM (0.00000 across 9/10 runs), and lower observed performance on dark-slick classes (WS, LWA) under uniform loss.
existing_evidence: Single-band VV SAR input provides scalar backscatter without polarization ratio (VH/VV) or multi-spectral contrast.
Wind streaks, biological slicks, and low wind areas share dark-backscatter characteristics in VV imagery.
Rain cells (RF) and point targets (HM) may exhibit low backscatter contrast against surrounding ocean background under standard log1p normalization.
prioritized_investigations.why_it_resolves_uncertainty: Quantifies empirical backscatter distributions (mean, variance, signal-to-clutter ratio, histogram overlap) within ground-truth mask polygons for all classes, measuring whether class-conditional backscatter distributions in single-channel VV SAR exhibit substantial overlap that could plausibly limit discriminability, without presuming an information bottleneck.
prioritized_investigations.compute_cost: Negligible CPU compute (NumPy statistical extraction on existing training GeoTIFFs).
prioritized_investigations.expected_information_value: High (evaluates distributional overlap directly from pixel evidence without speculative bottleneck assumptions).
prioritized_investigations.required_control: OPS-02 TRAIN and DEV raw rasters and ground-truth masks.
prioritized_investigations.required_data: Frozen OPS-02 derived images and masks.

prohibited_actions: Do NOT launch new GPU training runs before completing diagnostic audits.
Do NOT access Part III benchmark.
Do NOT adopt uniform weighting as canonical.
